Cruz, Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter, Kirby McInerney) have announced securities fraud investigations, following the roughly 13% fall in the stock on 8 May 2026 after the disclosure, in Q1 26, of a lengthening of the average loan duration in Brazil (5 to 8 months) and of an increase in bad debt provisions.

clesRetenues: Q Sgarz (Goldman Sachs, sequential gross margin compression, ability to pass on cost increases) - the CFO explains the sequentially stable margin through two offsetting effects: an improvement in Brazilian consumer credit (normalised provisions) offset by the Pix rebates/lower take rates in Brazil and the increase in device costs in Mexico (partly a one-off overstock); the CEO specifies that POS terminal prices have not been raised because the paybacks remain attractive and competitors have not moved.

Q Ruben (Morgan Stanley, acceleration in seller growth in Brazil +29% and effect on the margin) - the CEO says that lower take rates systematically stimulate the growth of high-performing sellers (already observed in 2024-2025) and that there is no significant margin impact tied to this specific acceleration.

Q Ford (BofA, read on the gamification/points programme in Brazil and on the agentic shopping pilot) - the CEO judges it too early to conclude on gamification (AB test under way, positive but unquantified impact); on agentic AI, he highlights gains already measurable in conversion and in advertising CTR through AI-assisted search.

Q Santos (JPMorgan, ramp-up of the credit card in Argentina) - the Fintech President says he is very satisfied with the pace of adoption (issuance started around nine months ago), too early to judge the paybacks but no negative surprise at this stage.

Q Galindo (Itau BBA, risk of a deterioration in the Brazilian credit cycle in H2) - the Fintech President confirms the absence of any sign of deterioration, NPLs close to their historical lows, and a proven ability to slow origination if necessary (already done in the past); the CEO adds that NPLs are close to their lows across practically all products/regions.

Q Pinto (Bradesco BBI, durability of the free shipping threshold effect in Brazil one year on, tougher comps) - the CFO and the CEO reaffirm that investment decisions are never driven by the comparison base but by the intrinsic merits of each initiative, and that the engagement gains (purchase frequency +20%, conversion +1,1pt) have proved durable and not a mere one-off effect.

Q Mathivanan (Cantor Fitzgerald, sustainability of the margin in H2 and breakdown of AI costs) - the CFO reaffirms the same disciplined investment philosophy (engagement and profitability targets by initiative, intensity modulated according to results) and quantifies the AI investment at around 80 M$ in Q2, with an already positive return on several consumer-side initiatives (search, seller assistant).

Q Araujo (Stifel, ramp-up of the affiliate programme) - the CEO reports growth in the share of affiliate GMV across all markets, materially higher platform retention among affiliate buyers, and stable unit economics as a % of sales despite the acceleration in investment.

Q Maurer (FT Partners, share of the memory price shock vs a deliberate decision in the Mexico margin compression, and whether the Mexican tax reform is already fully reflected in the growth rate) - the Fintech President attributes most of the compression to the one-off device overstock and to the increase in the cost of memory chips (not to a deliberate price cut); the CEO confirms that the Mexican tax reform remains a headwind in Q2, temporarily aggravated by a weaker macro environment and the World Cup.

Q Beck (Raymond James, return on AI investment and trend in credit card NIMAL by cohort) - the CFO specifies that most of the 1 point gain on product development costs does NOT come from AI but from earlier structural scale gains; the Fintech President says that each card cohort reaches NIMAL breakeven in 12 to 18 months, a pace that is stable over time.

Q Friedel (UBS, rise in 90+ day NPLs despite the improvement in 15-90 day NPLs) - the Fintech President attributes the rise in long NPLs to an origination slowdown in late 2025 tied to a one-off deterioration in certain early cohorts, a phenomenon judged not concerning and already unwinding; the CFO adds a mechanical duration effect (good payers exit the book quickly, defaulters stay in it for 360 days).

Q Aggarwal (HSBC, impact of the fall in Brazilian policy rates on the different segments) - the Fintech President reports a non-significant impact on acquiring and on credit (the rates applied follow the market); the CEO specifies a marginally positive effect on credit already issued (priced at a higher rate) and a more noticeable effect on the margin of the marketplace's parcelado sin juros, whose prices are not repriced as frequently.

Q Fong (BTIG, share of 'ecosystemic' users in the total base, strategy for monetising cross-border trade) - the CFO does not disclose the exact share of ecosystemic users but confirms it is the fastest-growing segment (+37% YoY); the CEO reports a continued sequential improvement in CBT unit economics over several quarters, driven by scale and operational learning.

Q Soares (Citi, credit card profitability trajectory, possible inflection point given the size of the book) - the Fintech President attributes the absence of a clear inflection to the average youth of the book (most of it issued over the last two years, cohorts older than three years marginal) rather than to a structural problem; the CEO points out that the profitability of the card alone understates its strategic value (ecosystemic effect of x2-3 on the probability of becoming an ecosystemic user).

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No formal quarterly guidance (no-guidance policy). Management signaled that H2 26 operating margin should stay near the H1 level (~6.7%): the Mexico POS-device restocking charge reverses over the rest of the year, while memory-chip cost inflation is 'there to stay'; investment intensity remains modulated initiative-by-initiative against engagement and profitability targets.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No formal FY guidance (no-guidance policy). Management explicitly refuses to steer investment by comparison bases ('we don't make investment decisions based on comps') and reaffirmed the same disciplined long-term reinvestment philosophy for H2 26 despite much tougher comps. Qualitative markers: credit-card cohorts reach NIMAL breakeven in 12-18 months; expected Brazil policy-rate cuts marginally positive for Marketplace take rates and broadly neutral for credit/acquiring; 2026 is the first year without engineering headcount growth as AI lifts developer productivity.
pointsCles: Net revenue crossed $10B in a single quarter for the first time ($10.17B, +50% YoY, +43% FX-neutral), with a broad-based Brazil acceleration one year after the free-shipping threshold cut (items per buyer +19% YoY, conversion +1.1pt, purchase frequency +20%, successful sellers +29%) and ecosystemic users (Marketplace + Mercado Pago) growing +37% YoY with +70% GMV and +90% TPV vs single-platform users.

EBIT margin of 6.7% was flat sequentially but down 550bp YoY - an explicitly deliberate reinvestment choice: gross-margin compression from Brazil take-rate cuts and PIX discounts, Mexico POS-device restocking (one-off, booked upfront at a loss) and memory-chip inflation, partly offset by normalized Brazil consumer-credit provisions after the Q1 spike and 2.5pts of QoQ OpEx dilution.

Credit portfolio reached $16.4B (+75% YoY) with NPLs near historical lows (15-90d at 7.0%, credit card at 4.6%) and consolidated NIMAL improving from 18% (Q1) to 21%; credit-card NIMAL of -2.5% reflects deliberately accelerated issuance (2.6M cards in Brazil in the quarter vs 1.6M a year earlier), with each cohort consistently reaching NIMAL breakeven in 12-18 months and Mexico paybacks better than Brazil.

AI investment of ~$80M in the quarter with measurable returns: product-development costs diluted from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenue, 90% of customer-service interactions handled without a human (7,000 reps vs 10,000 four years ago on a 3x larger business), AI search live in the 5 largest countries with net-positive ROI; advertising grew +73% YoY and cross-border GMV ~+60% with China fulfillment-center volume +170% QoQ.

hypothese.summary: Undisputed leader in e-commerce and fintech in Latin America, crossing 10 Md$ of quarterly revenue for the first time (+50% YoY). Operating margin held by deliberate choice at ~6,7% (vs ~11% in 2025 restated), with management reaffirming that it never steers its investments by the comps. Margin recovery expected gradually as the investments (Brazil shipping threshold, credit card, AI, CBT) reach maturity.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
MercadoLibre is the Latin American profitable-growth compounder: Q2 26 revenue crossed 10bn$ for the first time (10.17bn$, +50% reported, +43% cc) and the ecosystem flywheel keeps strengthening - a commerce+fintech user generates a MULTIPLE of the standalone contributions, and ecosystem users grew +37%. One year after the Brazil free-shipping threshold cut, the effect is proven durable and non-promotional (purchase frequency +19%, conversion +1.1pt, better cohort retention) - the central thesis anchor validated. Operating margin stays deliberately dialed down at 6.7% (flat sequentially, -550bp YoY) as management reinvests in Brazil delivery thresholds and credit-card issuance, explicitly refusing to steer by comparison bases. New this quarter: AI became a measured efficiency vector (product-dev cost 8.4% -> 7.2% of revenue, 90% of customer-service interactions automated, ~80M$/quarter invested) - the first concrete support for the 2027-2030 margin-recovery leg of the thesis. Classified as a financial issuer (bank): the credit book (16.4bn$, +75%) makes net debt a funding line, not leverage - multiples read on market cap.

== THESIS READ ==
- Revenue through 10bn$/quarter with Brazil +42% cc and Mexico +38% cc: growth is broad, not base-effect driven.
- Margin dial confirmed at 6.7% with the reinvestment explicitly deliberate - the recovery option (2027-2030) stays intact and now has an AI-efficiency down-payment.
- Brazil credit normalization delivered: NIMAL back to 20.7% (from 18% at the Q1 provisioning peak) - the event behind the May plaintiff-firm inquiries has resolved favorably (no complaint filed, >3 months).
- Credit book +75% to 16.4bn$ with NPL 15-90d at 7.0%: the growth/risk balance holds, tracked via the guided proxies (no group prudential ratio exists - see capitalConstraintNote).
- Watch: H2 margin against much tougher comps - management says the dial stays down; any early recovery would be pure upside to the modeled path.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: published US GAAP ('ca' = net revenues incl. financial income; 'ebit' = income from operations), USD. Data 2025 corrections (net 1,997, EBIT 3,201) were made at the 07/08 refresh from official figures. Bridge (c-ter): ETR 24% normative (S1 26 observed, ex one-off - ancrage etr_2026_2030) with finNet scaling with the credit-book funding (-275 -> -650M$; financial issuer: E5 a-bis industrial rules not applicable, funding is the business). Scorecard: no-guidance house - FY26 anchor posed on the own 22/07 vintage (imperfect, re-anchor Feb 2027), history not measurable, application suspended (documented); quarterly consensus beats tracked in the timeline (+2.7% Q2). Deprecated keys purged (C23). WATCH-LIST: (1) H2 operating margin vs tougher comps; (2) 90d+ NPL trajectory (slightly up, management unconcerned - verify); (3) plaintiff-firm inquiries (quiet >3 months); (4) Argentina credit-card paybacks (~9 months in, too early); (5) Mexico device-cost overstock fading in H2. Next useful refresh: Q3 results (28 Oct).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 (28 Oct): margin resilience against hard comps; credit-card and cross-border (GMV +60% cc, China fulfillment +170% QoQ) profitability signals.

ancrages.moteur: Free shipping threshold in Brazil lowered in 2025: one year on, the effect is confirmed as durable and not promotional (purchase frequency +19% YoY in Q2 26, conversion +1,1pt YoY, retention of the new cohorts higher than that of the previous ones) - a structural driver of revenue growth, kept as a durable margin compressor through the absorbed shipping cost.

H1 26 operating margin at 6,8% (Q1 6,9%, Q2 6,7%), stable sequentially despite an additional compression in gross margin (Pix rebates/take rates Brazil, device costs Mexico). Management explicitly reaffirms that it never steers its investments by comparison bases - the margin 'dial' is kept close to this level over H2 26 despite more demanding comps.

Combined impact of the strategic investments (free shipping, 1P, cross-border trade, credit card) originally quantified by management at 5-6 points of operating margin - serves as the anchor for the margin recovery trajectory projected over 2027-2030 as these investments reach maturity (no new quantification this quarter, anchor rolled forward without revision).

New anchor (Q2 26): AI investment quantified at ~80 M$/quarter (vs the prior year), with a first measurable effect on product R&D costs (8,4% -> 7,2% of revenue year-on-year, ~120bps) and on customer service automation (90% of interactions with no human intervention). The CFO specifies that most of this gain does not yet come from AI but from earlier scale gains - treated cautiously as a nascent and still partial tailwind, distinct from the maturation of the broader investments (investment_drag_quantified).

Lengthening of the average loan duration in Brazil (5 to 8 months) and increase in provisions flagged in Q1 26: NORMALISATION CONFIRMED in Q2 26 (consolidated NIMAL improved from 18% to 21%, Brazil NPLs stable at close to their lows). Event now positively resolved - anchor rolled forward with a revised mechanism (downside risk lifted for projected net income, unlike the previous refresh); credit card NIMAL remains negative (-2,5%) but is judged transitory (cohorts reaching breakeven in 12-18 months).

Rule E5-a bis: positive and rising net debt (6 425 M$ at 30/06/26, funding of the rapidly expanding credit book +75% YoY), no active buyback programme -> projected net financial charges = US 10Y Treasury (4,68% at 07/08/2026) + 2pts = 6,68%, applied to the projected average net debt of each year.

Effective tax rate revised from 29,7% (FY2025 base, including a one-off item already documented) to ~24%, anchored on the effective rate actually observed in H1 26 (302/1185=25,5% in H1, 140/606=23,1% in Q2 alone - more recent and with no known one-off, unlike the FY2025 base).

One-off tax credit of 99 M$ in Brazil (Q4 25), explicitly designated as a one-off by management - already excluded from the restated FY2025 base (see the data correction in E1/PARAMETRES); historical anchor kept for traceability, with no impact on the 2026+ projection.

capitalConstraintNote: MELI group is not a prudentially consolidated bank: no group-level CET1/solvency ratio is published. Credit risk is tracked through the guided proxies instead - NPL 15-90d (7.0% Q2 26), NIMAL (20.7%), Brazil provisioning (see ancrage brazil_credit_provisioning). Subsidiary licenses (Mexico bank, Brazil SCFI) publish local ratios that do not consolidate at group level. Revisit if prudential consolidation ever applies.
